newsitem.title: UK: Russia Urals, Nigerian grades steady on demand.
newsitem.headline: Russia Urals, Nigerian grades steady on demand.

text.p: Russian Urals seemed to be holding steady in a "very private and confidential" Mediterranean market on Thursday, and traders said light West African crudes were also buoyed by recent Asian buying interest.

In a quiet Mediterranean market, traders said that Urals was assessed in the Dated Brent -$1.15 to -$1.10 cif region. This compared with deals reported last week at prices as low as Dated Brent -$1.29 and -$1.35.
"There is not a lot of alternative sour (crudes)... The alternative is usually Iranian but it seems to be sold out from May, possibly also June," a Mediterranean refiner said.

"There was also a Greek tender (yesterday) for sour crude and some Urals went to the tender," the refiner said, adding Urals was also drawing strength from a brief shut down of Russia's main Novorossissk port for repair work next week.

"We've had very p+c (private and confidential) deals recently, not a great deal of names or numbers, because unless your are really trying to buy something it is difficult to know," the refiner added.

Traders said negotiations between term lifters and Syria's state oil company Sytrol begin on Thursday for June prices, with the Syrians asking for a higher Dated Brent -60 cents for Syrian Light compared with May's OSP of Dated Brent -82 cents.

The official selling price (OSP) for loadings of May Syrian Light was agreed at that level after lengthy negotiations with the term lifters, who were seeking a rollover of April's Dated Brent -95 cents into May.
"The negotiations will begin today," one Italian refiner said.
"The telex just landed on my desk. The Syrians are asking Dated Brent -60 cents for Syrian Light," a trader of Mediterranean crude said.
It was not immediately known what Sytrol was asking for its Souedie grade. The OSP for Souedie was set at Dated Brent -$4.65 in May, a little bit stronger than April's Dated Brent -$4.70.

Traders said there may be cancellation of one or two May cargoes of Iraqi Kirkuk, due to the recent rise in crude prices which pushes the limit on the amount of barrels that Baghdad can export under the oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.

West African traders said no deals were reported early on Thursday, adding light Nigerian grades were holding on to current hight levels, with Bonny Light assessed at a premium of some 55 cents to Dated Brent.
"The grades were being pushed up by the fact that May cargoes, even some early June barrels, have already found homes.
"They going to the Far East and the United States mainly, some to Europe," a European trader of West African crude said.
In Tokyo, leading Japanese refiner Cosmo Oil said on Thursday it had purchased a volume comparable to a very large crude carrier (VLCC) of Bonny Light crude for May-lifting.

The company said the crude was priced Dated related but declined to be more specific. However, one West African crude trader said the price was Dated Brent +35 cents and that the deal was done on April 17.
"It's well below today's price levels (for African sweet crudes)," the trader said.
A Cosmo spokesman said Bonny Light crude was bought because of a recently narrow Brent/Dubai spread which make West African grades a financially attractive choice.
The discount of Asian benchmark Dubai crude to North Sea bellwether Dated Brent is the primary trigger for the flow of Brent-linked crudes into Asia.
-- Haitham Haddadin, London newsroom +44 171 542 8145
